note: Faithful rendering of the svabhāvahetu/kāryahetu argument and the summarising verses; the anthill gloss on śakramūrdhan is inline but correct.
Accurate rendering of the cetanā/cetayitvā commentary with verses correctly set off; inline glosses are clumsy but not wrong.

errors.english: not distributing the robes of the monastic community
errors.why: In context (rain without cover, washing, dyeing, splitting wood, on the previous side) བགོ་བ here means wearing the saṃgha's robes, not distributing them.

note: A difficult Vinayasūtra commentary rendered sensibly overall; the opening misreads 'not wearing' the saṃgha's robes as 'not distributing'.

errors.english: (Kumarila) [note: refers to the Mimamsa scholar Kumarila Bhatta]
errors.why: Nothing in སྐྱེས་མོས supports identifying the speaker as Kumārila (Tibetan gzhon nu ma len); the identification is speculative and presented as fact.

errors.english: existence itself is not apparent because it is void of and separated from "the other."
errors.why: The Tibetan says existence does not appear apart from (dang bral bas) the form that is void of others, i.e. it appears only as that exclusion; the English makes existence itself void of and separated from the other.

errors.english: is intended to be the producer of its own aspect
errors.why: མངོན་པར་སེམས་པ here is the cognition's (mistaken) conceiving/imputing (cf. mngon par rlom pa on the next side), not 'intending'; so too 'nothing other than what is intended' should be 'nothing other than this conceiving'.

note: The dream/waking and non-existence-cognition argument is followed in outline, but several clauses of the apoha-style reasoning are misparsed and an unsupported attribution is added.

errors.english: While it is established as observed because it is not obstructed even if not experienced
errors.why: བསྐལ་བ is viprakṛṣṭa, 'remote/inaccessible' (the three remotenesses of place, time and nature), not 'obstructed'; the same error runs through 'three kinds of obstruction' and 'the unobstructed aspect of inference'.

fix.find: While it is established as observed because it is not obstructed even if not experienced
fix.replace: While it is established as observed because, even if not experienced, it is not remote (viprakṛṣṭa)

note: The dravya/guṇa section is sound, but the key Pramāṇa term for remoteness (viprakarṣa) is systematically rendered as 'obstruction' in the opening paragraph.

errors.english: because there is no intention, and because it is not the proper basis
errors.why: The Tibetan says that without abhijñā (mngon par shes pa) it is not the [proper] field; 'no intention' is not in the text, and ཡིད་མི་ཆེས་པའི་སེམས ('a mind that does not trust/believe') is then rendered as 'without a deceitful mind'.

errors.english: if the carrier positioned on land within the border has no need for it, there is no infraction. However, if the carrier positioned on land within the border does have a need, it constitutes a grave offense.
errors.why: The Tibetan says: where the mantra/medicine needs no carrier standing on land inside the boundary there is no offence; where there is a carrier standing on land inside the boundary it is a sthūlātyaya. The English makes it the carrier's 'need' and adds 'does have a need'.

note: The customs-evasion (śulka) rulings are mostly clear, but the closing distinctions on magical carrying are misconstrued.
Faithful rendering of the Mahāyāna-authenticity argument against the Vaibhāṣikas, with the patriarch lineage and the parity argument correctly attributed.
Accurate rendering of the general/specific and indirect/direct characteristics of the truths and the two kinds of seekers of liberation.

errors.english: where the reason exists in all instances of the property to be proven
errors.why: Anvaya is the presence of the probandum pervading the presence of the reason in every case (wherever the reason, there the probandum); the English inverts the pervasion.

fix.find: where the reason exists in all instances of the property to be proven
fix.replace: in which, in every case, the presence of the property to be proven pervades the presence of the reason

errors.english: the presence of the reason wherever the property is present
errors.why: The inline gloss on anvaya states the converse; positive concomitance is the presence of the property to be proven wherever the reason is present.

fix.find: the presence of the reason wherever the property is present
fix.replace: the presence of the property wherever the reason is present

errors.english: establishes the connection between the concordant class and the non-concordant class as previously explained
errors.why: The pramāṇa establishes the relation (between reason and probandum), and its existence is what makes the presence/absence in sapakṣa and vipakṣa as described established; there is no 'connection between the concordant and non-concordant class'.

note: The argument for 'certainty' (niścaya) in the trairūpya definition is followed, but anvaya is inverted both in a gloss and in the body, and the closing clause is misconstrued.
A sound rendering of the close of the first saṃghāvaśeṣa analysis and the commentary on the stages of emission and sthūlātyaya.
